audit: The 30 places are distinct new sites, not route interpolation points. Existing City Hall and Lincoln Heights Jail sites are not duplicated.
The Shield’s Barn was investigated but omitted: the original church and later studio replica do not establish a strong precise story pin in fictional Farmington.
The Nice Guys LA Auto Show, Sid Shattuck mansion, adult theater and police-station material filmed in Atlanta are excluded despite their L.A. story setting.

Colors’ final raid follows the 2023 location-manager interview at Figueroa Terrace. The older guide’s Vista Hermosa guess is rejected.

Last Boy Scout: AFI’s production history reports the climax at the Coliseum with 6,000 extras. The Cleveland opening setting is excluded. IMDb also lists San Diego Stadium; its differing component claim is not used to assert that the climax occurred outside L.A.
House/site images are dated only when evidence states capture dates. 2011 Hallenbeck and 2007 Coliseum images are archival, clearly captioned. Hallenbeck house was destroyed in the 2025 fire.
Global Film Locations site pairs are undated Google Street View images, not assertions of current appearance. Covina Bowl’s image precedes closure/redevelopment.
Ilena’s movie-side picture is an expressly captioned screen/site comparison from L.A. TACO, not a standalone frame; site side uses active-basemap aerial.
Jordan Downs point is a community-level location; the exact grandparents’ unit is not asserted and 2018 site imagery predates redevelopment.
AFI locates Marcone’s fatal explosion below Griffith Observatory, so his mansion uses an editorial Los Feliz / Hollywood Hills pin; San Marino is production provenance only.

audit.verification: The film’s mail gives 901 Drury Lane, Beverly Hills. The Encino house is the production exterior and interior, not the story address. Drury Lane’s representative point is an editorial street estimate; no canonical parcel is asserted.

Bronson Alcott is the fictional Beverly Hills high school. Occidental College supplies the campus exteriors; additional interiors were shot at Grant High School. This estimated Beverly Hills point does not identify a real school parcel.
The Las Palmas Hotel exterior and fire escape establish Vivian and Kit’s Hollywood apartment. Production street retained as the uncontradicted exterior proxy.
The named Beverly Wilshire plays Edward’s hotel. The point identifies the Wilshire hotel frontage; hotel interiors also used other production components.

Dialogue names the restaurant the Voltaire. The filmed dining room was Rex Il Ristorante, now Cicada, in the Oviatt Building; no canonical street address is given. The physical dining room supplies the proxy.

The fictional Blue Banana combines a dressed 6708 Hollywood Boulevard storefront with the interior and rear entrance of 4067 West Pico Boulevard. The Hollywood exterior anchors the story club; the Pico component is not a second club.
Edward’s Los Angeles workplace and lawn are filmed at Bank of America Plaza, 333 South Hope Street. No separate canonical business street is established.
The Canadian Building supplies Tom’s apartment exterior; Fenton Building supplies interiors. The Main Street exterior is the proxy for his fictional home, not the production address of the interior.

The apartment was filmed at the Barclay on Normandie, but the visible downtown skyline was composited. This central-Los-Angeles estimate acknowledges the impossible production view; the canonical neighborhood and street are unresolved.

Angels Knoll supplies the bench and the recognizable downtown view. The film calls it Angelus Plaza; the nearby real senior-housing complex is not substituted for the bench site. The point uses the documented park location, not a street-geocoder interpolation.
The story karaoke bar is called the Mill. The Redwood Bar & Grill supplies the matched interior; no contrary canonical street has been established.

The named Civic Center fountain appears in Tom’s dance sequence and in Vivian and Edward’s walk. MovieMaps supplies the downtown fountain point; the same-name geocoder result in Monrovia was rejected.
The Los Angeles Conservancy identifies the Fenton Building as the greeting-card workplace. It also supplied apartment interiors; these are separate fictional places with separate exterior anchors.

Amanda’s house is in Brentwood near Arthur’s home in the screenplay and story. The exterior was filmed in San Marino. This broad Brentwood estimate preserves their neighborhood relationship without inventing a street or claiming an adjacent parcel.
The screenplay places Arthur in Brentwood, consistent with the 163 South Rockingham filming house. That street address remains a filming proxy, not a spoken canonical address.
Iris and Miles visit a Brentwood Blockbuster. Matched windows, entrance and street trees identify the former 11770 San Vicente store; the bank conversion photograph is labeled archival.

Mia walks through Chinatown immediately before visiting Sebastian at night. This editorial Chinatown-area estimate follows that story cue; it is not a confirmed neighborhood or address. The courtyard was filmed at 8404 Willis Avenue in Panorama City, kept as production provenance.

The dance overlook was filmed at Cathy’s Corner on Mount Hollywood Drive. The source identifies this specific viewpoint; the bench, lamppost and parked cars were production additions. No drivable walking route from the party is inferred.
Sebastian sings on Hermosa Beach Pier. The point is on the actual pier, using the City’s project coordinates rather than the inaccurate rounded GeoNames meteorological-station point.
The recognizable Angels Flight railway appears in Mia and Sebastian’s summer montage. The marker identifies its upper station, not an invented journey beyond the railway.
Mia and Sebastian eat inside Grand Central Market during their summer montage. The named market is retained as the story place.

Seb’s is a composite: Hollywood storefront at 6202 Santa Monica Boulevard and interior at the Blind Donkey, 149 Linden Avenue, Long Beach. The exterior anchors one fictional Hollywood club; the interior is not mapped as another club.

The production designer documents the existing Valley house and its dressed kitchen; the address is identified by specialist location research. With no conflicting canonical street established, its physical exterior supplies the proxy.
The production designer documents Alana’s family house in the Valley; matched location research identifies the Miranda Street property. No exact canonical street is asserted.
The production designer identifies the Chatsworth storefront conversion from waterbed shop to pinball arcade. Both businesses share one story premises and are one map place.

The production designer describes conversion of a local storefront into Wachs’s campaign office; location research identifies 21702 Sherman Way. This is the film office, not a claim about the politician’s actual historical headquarters.

The production designer confirms that the Tudor house and steep driveway were used for Jon Peters’s scenes. The Encino production house is retained as a proxy; the montage’s Tarzana roads do not move this house to every stunt location.

The film names the historic Valley restaurant Tail o’ the Cock. The museum and city history place it at 12950 Ventura Boulevard, Studio City. Its room was recreated at Billingsley’s, 6550 Odessa Avenue, Van Nuys. The marker follows the named story venue; the production replica remains separately credited.
